title: Technical Credibility Flashcards (WIP)
body:
Purpose: Short, punchy flashcards for SEs and field engineers to use during quick pre-call prep and in-the-moment rebuttals. This is intentionally terse — memorisable lines + 2–3 backup facts to defend claims. Draft for peer review; want 40–50 cards total (this doc contains a first 18).

TL;DR elevator lines (1-2 sentences each)
- Why Redwood for production inference: "Predictable performance + built-in fallbacks = fewer outages and lower unpredictable cost." (backup: dedicated pools, canary rollouts, autoscaling controls).
- Why not build your own: "Engineering cost and ops overhead scale superlinearly; we provide kernel-optimized runtimes and routing logic that teams rarely replicate cheaply." (backup: maintenance, ops headcount, compilers/kernels).

Flashcard format: front = one-line prompt the rep can say; back = 2–3 bullet backup facts + quick metric or example.

Cards (front -> back):
1) "Latency budget too tight?" -> "Use Dedicated + autoscale-in-place; can pin low-latency kernels and reduce p95 by 20–40%. Example: fintech pilot reduced p95 from 420ms -> 270ms after moving to dedicated + prefix cache (internal benchmark GT-MKT-881)."

2) "How do we control per-token cost?" -> "Batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantized variants. Typical savings: 15–50% depending on request shape; mobile chat workloads saw ~30% reduction by enabling prefix cache + eager batching."

3) "Fallbacks if a model is down" -> "Automated routing to compatible variants (quantized / smaller model) with graceful degradation; SLA horseshoe: user stays served while quality is monitored and spike alerts trigger rollbacks."

4) "Data privacy for PII workloads" -> "Private (VPC) with customer KMS + audit logs; option for on-prem air-gapped deployment and HSM integration for regulated customers."

5) "How to avoid hallucinations in retrieval apps" -> "Combine retrieval-augmented generation with reranking + model calibration checks. We surface confidence signals and can route low-confidence answers to a 'human review' flow."

6) "What does 'quantization-friendly' runtime mean?" -> "Runtime uses kernels optimized for int8/fp16 and reorders ops to keep KV cache performance; reduces memory footprint and enables higher concurrency on same GPU."

7) "Can you A/B test model rollouts?" -> "Yes — per-route rollout policies with traffic splits, canary windows, automatic regression monitors tied to eval prompt sets."

8) "What about spikes / burst traffic?" -> "Reserved Dedicated capacity + burst buffers; for hosted customers we recommend hybrid reserved + burst pool to smooth over seasonal peaks."

9) "How do we measure quality regressions?" -> "Prompt-set based evals, live sampling, and automatic regression alerts; tie regression to model version and prompt set for quick rollback."

10) "Will we need to change prompts between variants?" -> "Sometimes — we provide sample 'variant-safe' prompts and a prompt-diffing tool that highlights behaviour changes across model versions."

11) "Security compliance: what standards?" -> "SOC2 in progress / ISO roadmap (specify customer-specific controls via Private deployments); we can provide artifacts early under NDA."

12) "Latency-vs-cost tuning play" -> "Two knobs: batch window and quantization target. Small increase in p50 (5–15ms) often gives big cost wins; show example trade curve during call."

13) "Edge/Private vs Hosted: when to pick?" -> "Pick Hosted for speed/POC; Dedicated for predictable high throughput; Private for regulatory/latency region needs. Use the routing policy to mix them in prod."

14) "How do we diagnose token-level latency spikes?" -> "Per-token traces in Console, token waterfall view, and trace links to infra metrics. Quick triage: check KV hit rate, kernel fallback, and batch sizes."

15) "What does support look like for Dedicated customers?" -> "SLA-backed on-call, runbook access, quarterly performance reviews; escalation path in Console + named SE for onboarding."

16) "Model compatibility story" -> "We maintain a compatibility matrix and automated conversion pipelines; when a new model has nonstandard ops we surface a compatibility grade and recommended runtime flags."

17) "Example pitch: GenAI in search (30s)" -> "Hook: 'Cut user search time in half while improving relevance.' How: RAG + reranker + token-level caching (demo numbers: 2x relevance score lift in internal POC). Ask: 'How many queries/min do you need to support?'"

18) "Quick rebuttal to 'we can use cloud provider endpoints'" -> "You can, but providers often lack unified routing, prefix caching, and per-token economics visibility — we give per-route cost breakdown and unit economics so product decisions are measurable."

Presentation skeleton (for deck conversion)
- Slide 1: 1-line positioning + one-sentence value prop (speaker note: start with customer pain).
- Slide 2: Flashcard set overview (how to use cards).
- Slide 3–7: Top 5 objection cards + examples (one per slide).
- Slide 8: Quick demo script + expected metrics (p95/p50/cost).
- Slide 9: Call to action + recommended next step (POC template).

Open questions / TODOs (peer review items)
- Add 22 more cards covering compliance objections and procurement play.
- Validate numbers with infra team (Liam to confirm p95 reductions per kernel).
- Add one-page POC checklist and minimal telemetry items.

Notes to self: keep language actionable and avoid marketing fluff; goal is fast recall in call. Link to POC template: confluence:GT-MKT-881.

Example short scripts for SEs (30–60s)
- "If latency is the blocker: 'We typically recommend Dedicated for critical paths — it reduced p95 by ~30% in a payments pilot; we'll set a canary and measure before cutover.'"
- "If cost is the blocker: 'Let's profile your token shape and enable prefix caching/batching — our Optimize toolkit gives a projected cost curve in under a day.'"

Appendix (facts & citations)
- Internal benchmark report: GT-MKT-881 (ops summary, kernel perf table).
- Case study: Fintech pilot (redacted): p95 420->270ms and 28% cost saving after dedicated+cache.
- Eval artifacts: sample prompt sets (linked in confluence).

Revision history: 2025-11-02 initial draft by Maya; 2025-12-08 added cards 9-12 (Priya); 2026-02-15 updated trade numbers and added script snippets (Liam).

Slack threads worth reading: #g2m-seedlist (context on objections), #infra-kernels (kernel perf debate).

Reviewer asks: please flag any claims that need data backing or phrasing that is too marketing-y. I want these to scan fast (one-liners + 2 backups).

End of draft.
